note: While clava hypertrophy occurs in ~24% of ACBD6 patients, it is a well-established hallmark of infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (an NBIA subtype), contradicting the claim that it is pathognomonic or absent in NBIA.

evidence.text: Hypertrophy of the clava was identified in 24% (5/21) of individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings

evidence.text: Clava hypertrophy is a recognized imaging feature of infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (INAD/PLA2G6), a major neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorder, present in 8/8 evaluated patients.

source.title: Validation of the finding of hypertrophy of the clava in infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy/PLA2G6 by biometric analysis
source.quote: Infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (INAD), an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder due to PLA2G6 mutation, is classified both as a PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration (PLAN) disorder and as one of the neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders. Age of onset and clinical presentation in INAD is variable... MRI, available in eight, showed clava hypertrophy, regardless of age
